title: Data Visualization Assignment
text: This analysis uses Office for National Statistics data following state-school pupils who took their GCSEs in 2012-2013, with educational records extending from primary school to age 22. It focuses on small, medium, and large towns across eight English regions. Higher income deprivation indicates greater hardship linked to low income.

title: Data Visualization Assignment
text:
Version A: Scientific Article

1.Box plot
Within all eight regions, median town education scores increase from higher to lower income deprivation categories. However, the score distributions overlap, indicating variation in educational attainment within each category.











2.Dumbbell plot
Lower-deprivation towns have higher mean education scores than higher-deprivation towns in every region, with each town weighted equally. The difference is largest in the North East and smallest in the South West, showing that the magnitude of the within-region disparity varies geographically.

2.Stacked Bar Chart
The North East has the highest share of higher-deprivation towns, at about 77%, while Yorkshire and The Humber and the North West both have shares around 55%. These percentages compare towns rather than residents, raising the next question: do regions with larger shares also have lower average education scores?











3.Scatter plot
The North East has the highest higher-deprivation share and the lowest average town education score, but the North West and Yorkshire and The Humber have similar shares and very different scores. Regional deprivation shares therefore do not consistently track educational attainment; these comparisons describe patterns rather than establish cause and effect.









In summary, these findings highlight the importance of examining income deprivation and educational attainment both within and across regions. Higher-deprivation towns have lower average education scores within every region, but regional deprivation shares alone do not explain differences in overall educational attainment.
